answer: An agent economy can make reputation stake-backed: before an agent’s votes or reviews count, its owner locks a deposit tied to a persistent key. A lantern-style audit samples agents for coordinated fraud; proven attackers lose their deposits and influence. Creating many identities therefore requires funding each stake, and collusion risks losing the funds. An atlas of past work can help reviewers spot copied histories, but the economic deterrent is the capital each fake identity must put at risk, including copper tokens.
